title: gpu-nsight-occupancy-analysis-2026-04-10
content:
Summary:

This is a working note capturing recent NVIDIA Nsight runs focused on GPU utilization and SM occupancy for the serving runtime. Runs targeted A100 and H100 instances while exercising the streaming generation path, attention KV cache updates, and our CUDA-graph capture flow. The goal: explain persistent low occupancy spikes we saw under mid-size batch workloads (batch=4-16), identify hot kernels, and propose mitigations (kernel fusion, async memcpy tuning, batching/prefill heuristics).

Test matrix (short):
- Models: 7B decoder-only (current serving build, fp16, q8/4 in some runs)
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, NVIDIA H100-SXM-80GB (separate runs)
- Workloads: streaming single-token requests, prefills with seq_len=256, 512; batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16
- Runtime flags: cuda-graph enabled/disabled, async-copy enabled, KV-cache on GPU, continuous batching on
- Tools: NVIDIA Nsight Systems 2025.3 and Nsight Compute for kernel-level metrics

Key observations:
1) Low SM occupancy despite high device memory utilization:
- Several kernels show poor achieved_occupancy (~15-30%) on A100 for our flash attention and matmul kernels at short sequence lengths (<=256). Memory footprint is high (KV cache + activations) but SM utilization is low: points to latency-bound kernels with insufficient parallelism for current launch configuration.
- H100 runs showed slightly better occupancy (25-40%) because of better tensor core utilization for our matmul kernels, but we still observed underutilized warps during small batch streaming scenarios.

2) Kernel timeline fragmentation around KV-cache update:
- Nsight timeline shows bursts: matmul -> kv_cache_update (small memcpy+indexing kernels) -> layernorm -> gelu -> small matmuls. The small indexing/memcpy-like kernels are dominant contributors to tail latency and prevent long-running compute kernels from amortizing launch overhead.
- CUDA API calls frequently interleave with kernels when cudaGraph is disabled; enabling cudaGraph reduced CPU->GPU launch chatter but highlighted that some kernels are too short to benefit from graphing (overhead still measurable).

3) Warp execution efficiency and divergent branches in flash attention kernel: 
- Nsight Compute reports warp_execution_efficiency at ~60-70% for attention kernels under seq_len=512, indicating divergence in conditional logic inside our custom attention kernels (padding handling, causal masking branches).

4) Host-side stalls correlated with memcpy syncs: 
- There are repeated small cudaMemcpyAsync jobs for KV updates when KV cache is partially on CPU in some experimental runs; these force short device stalls and serialization points visible in the Nsight timeline.

Detailed kernel hotspots (top contributors by total GPU time across runs):
- matmul_gemm_fp16 (cuBLAS/TensorCore matmuls): main compute, high throughput when batch and seq_len allow large GEMMs
- flash_attn_kernel: significant time, but low occupancy on short seq_len runs; shows divergent control flow
- kv_cache_update_kernel: many small launches, dominated by memory ops and indexing, high kernel launch/serialize overhead
- layernorm_forward / layernorm_backward: moderately sized kernels with reasonable occupancy but frequent launches add overhead
- gelu_approx / activation kernels: short-lived, many small calls in sequence

Hypotheses (why occupancy is low):
- Small problem sizes per kernel (short seq lengths and small batch sizes) lead to low thread block counts and hence low SM occupancy.
- Branch-heavy attention implementation for masking introduces warp divergence and reduces throughput.
- KV-cache update path uses many small kernels and small async memcpys; those small kernels dominate overhead despite low per-call time.
- CUDA graph captures help reduce CPU-side overhead but do not increase per-kernel occupancy; they expose that some kernels are simply too small.

Quick experiments run during profiling session:
- Merged small memcpy kernels into larger batched memcpy: reduced number of launches by ~40% and improved end-to-end token latency by ~6% for batch=8 seq=256 on A100.
- Enabled cudaGraph for the forward-only generation path: CPU->GPU launch time reduced ~35% for sustained streaming load, but tail latency improvement was modest (~4%) because short kernels still serialized due to dependencies.
- Increased compute tile sizes in attention kernel (more threads per block) in a dev branch: occupancy rose by 10 percentage points but introduced register pressure which increased local memory spills on A100; net latency improved slightly for seq_len>=512 but regressed for seq_len=128.

Recommended mitigations (short term):
1) Batch small KV-cache updates: combine multiple per-token updates into a single kernel launch when possible. This change already shows ~6% latency improvement in quick tests.
2) Prioritize cudaGraph for hot steady-state paths (inference-only graph per model+seq_len+batch combo) to remove CPU launch jitter. Keep fallback for dynamic function calling or tool-calls.
3) Add a short-seq fast-path: for seq_len<=256 and batch<=8 use a lighter-weight attention kernel optimized for small shapes (reduce branching, precompute masks on GPU) to improve warp efficiency.
4) Investigate attention kernel refactor to reduce divergence: replace per-thread branching with warp-level predicate masks where possible.
5) Avoid GPU<->CPU memcpy for KV when latency-sensitive; keep KV fully on device or use pinned host buffers with larger aggregated transfers.

Longer-term ideas:
- Kernel fusion: fuse layernorm+GELU+linear where possible to reduce small kernel launches and memory round-trips. Prototype showed promising reductions in launches but increases in code complexity and register pressure must be measured across A100/H100.
- Dynamic autotuner: at runtime pick kernel variants based on observed seq_len and batch distributions (lightweight vs heavy kernels).
- Explore cooperative groups / warp-aggregated launches to increase occupancy for small sizes.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need controlled A/B on H100 with fused kernels to measure whether H100 register pressure favors fusion more than A100.
- Measure impact of increased occupancy on power/TDP and unit cost; higher occupancy may increase energy per token in some cases.
- Validate that batching KV updates does not materially increase memory pressure or cause GC-like spikes during long sessions.

Action items (owners):
- Michael Chen: land KV-update batching prototype in feature branch; add unit tests + perf harness (ETA 2026-04-16).
- Priya Nair: produce Nsight timelines for H100 fused vs unfused kernels (ETA 2026-04-18).
- Luca Rossi: implement small-seq fast-path kernel skeleton and run internal benchmark suite (ETA 2026-04-20).
- TODO: Add a dashboard card in Redwood Console for per-kernel occupancy and warp efficiency per model (linked artifact: CONFLUENCE-RT-occupancy-notes-2026).

Notes to self / debugging tips:
- When you run Nsight, turn off sampling on other processes (e.g., monitoring agents): small background jobs distort short-kernel metrics.
- Use Nsight compute to capture per-kernel metrics (achieved_occupancy, warp_efficiency, gf_ops_utilization) and then Nsight Systems for cross-kernel timeline correlation.
- For cudaGraph experiments, capture graph with nvprof-style trace to ensure capture contains expected async memcpy ordering.

Appendix (quick commands used):
- Nsight Systems capture: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o run_a100_seq256_batch8 ./serve_bench --model 7b --seq 256 --batch 8 --cuda-graph
- Nsight Compute: ncu --metrics achieved_occupancy,warp_execution_efficiency,sm_active_cycles --target-processes all --kernel-id ::regex:flash_attn_kernel ./serve_bench

If you find additional anomalies in other runs (e.g., sudden jumps in SM utilization or long memcpy stalls), drop logs and Nsight exports in the channel #eng-serving-runtime-profiling.

References:
- Internal perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/432
- Jira ticket for tail latency investigation: JIRA-RT-789

Status: working draft; will convert to Confluence summary once short-term mitigations are validated.
